Subject: Unified unit mapping and minimums — BrightLabs deal

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion I attached a compact mapping matrix that shows how we map requests to billing units for the proposed SKU mix. High-level summary here: 

- Billing unit: 25-token quantum for per-token SKUs (round up).
- Streaming responses: billed by 5-token chunk with a 1-chunk minimum per streamed response.
- Long-context reads (context > 16k): counted as separate ingest tokens then bucketed by the 25-token quantum, with prefix caching credited after the second identical prefix hit.

I've attached "unit_mapping_matrix.xlsx" with worked examples from the BrightLabs sample workload you shared (search + multi-turn chat + summarization). Please review the examples on rows 12–20 — they map your sample calls to invoice-line equivalents.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the 25-token quantum + 5-token streaming chunking is acceptable.
2) We'll add an initial smoothing concession (one-month buffer credit) if you go ahead with the pilot.
3) If procurement is comfortable, we can update the proposal and send the DocuSign link.

Open to tweaks — wanted to get a clear, auditable rule set in writing so your billing team can reconcile sample invoices easily.

Thanks,

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the matrix and the call recap. A couple of clarifying questions from our finance/procurement side before we proceed: 

1) Rounding/aggregation: The example invoice you sent earlier showed two separate calls billed as 4 units total which felt higher than our expected amortized cost. Can you show the math for a multi-turn session where we stream interim responses and then a final summarize call (similar to our sample user flow)? Specifically, we need to know whether streaming chunks get rounded independently or if the session-level aggregation reduces rounding overhead.

2) Minimums: What is the absolute per-call minimum in practice? For low-volume helper endpoints we see many short calls and want to avoid being overcharged by per-call minimums.

3) Trial smoothing: Procurement asked whether you can offer any smoothing credits for the first two months while we ramp usage patterns — that will make forecasting simpler for our accountants.

If it's easiest, loop in someone from pricing/ops to provide a short worked example.

Best,
Laura Chen

Subject: Fwd: Unified unit mapping and minimums — BrightLabs deal

Team — forwarding Laura's procurement questions. Customer wants a clear worked example + asks for smoothing concession for ramp. Comments inline below and a recommended customer-facing text. See also the attached matrix for per-call math.

QUICK ANSWERS (draft):
- Rounding/Aggregation: We apply tokenization at request time to both prompt + completion. For streaming responses we emit billing events per 5-token chunk. Billing aggregation occurs at a session/window level when requests are part of the same conversation id and within a 30s inter-message window — then we coalesce chunk-level events into the nearest 25-token quantum at the invoice line level to avoid double-counting short bursts.

- Minimums: Our effective per-call minimum is 25 tokens (one quantum) unless streaming where a 1-chunk (5-token) floor applies. Practically that means a short helper reply that streams 1 chunk is billed as 1 chunk (5 tokens), but a non-streamed short completion will round up to 25 tokens. This hybrid rule reduces friction for streaming-heavy integrations.

- Trial smoothing concession: propose a 2-month ramp smoothing credit equal to the difference between actual billed tokens and an amortized projected usage floor (cap at $5k). This is limited to pilot customers and only applies once.

WORKED EXAMPLES (put this in the customer reply):
1) Single short non-streamed completion (user prompt 12 tokens, completion 8 tokens = 20 total): rounds up to 25 tokens -> billed as 1 unit (25).
2) Streaming short reply (prompt 12, first streaming chunk 5 tokens returned): billed as 1 chunk (5 tokens) because streaming floor applies. If user continues and total completion reaches 28 tokens over 6 chunks, session aggregation then coalesces to 50 tokens (2 quanta) on invoice.
3) Multi-turn session with prefix reuse: if same 512-token prefix is reused across calls, after the first full ingest the subsequent identical prefixes are credited (we only bill delta tokens) — see spreadsheet rows 15–18.

We should confirm two negotiation levers before I reply to Laura:
A) Cap the smoothing credit at $5k vs $10k? Recommend $5k for this mid-market profile.
B) Limit streaming-chunk floor only to connections that use streaming API (prevents abuse).

Marcus/Kim: quick sanity check on the aggregation window and the math (I pulled the numbers from the matrix but want an ops sign-off). Vanessa: ok to offer a 2-month smoothing capped at $5k as pilot concession?

Thanks — R

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear questions — we took a pass at concise rules + worked examples so your finance team has something auditable. I've pasted the short version below and attached an updated proposal PDF (BrightLabs_proposal_v1.pdf) with the pilot concession baked in. If this looks good we can send the DocuSign link.

Finalized rules (customer-facing):
- Token quantum: 25 tokens per billing unit for non-streamed calls (always round up).
- Streaming chunking: billed per 5-token chunk; a 1-chunk minimum applies to every streamed response.
- Session aggregation: when multiple requests share the same conversation_id within a rolling 30s window, we aggregate tokens before applying 25-token rounding (this reduces churn from quick back-and-forths).
- Prefix caching: identical prefix ingestion is credited after the first full ingest; only delta tokens bill thereafter.
- Trial smoothing concession: for the first 60 days after go-live Redwood will apply a one-time smoothing credit up to $5,000 to offset rounding overhead while you ramp.

Worked example (mirrors the attachment rows 12–16):
- Scenario: user sends a 14-token prompt; server streams a 6-token partial reply (1 chunk) then continues to stream another 22 tokens (total streamed completion 28 tokens => 6 chunks).
- Billing: initial 6-token chunk billed as 1 chunk (5 tokens floor applies) then remaining streamed chunks billed and aggregated within session window. Total billed tokens after aggregation = 30 tokens -> rounds to 50 tokens invoiced (2 x 25-token quanta).

If you prefer we can change the quantum size, but 25 tokens is our standard that balances invoice granularity with ease of reconciliation.

Next steps:
1) If procurement signs off, we'll attach the updated SOW + proposal and send DocuSign (link included in the proposal PDF).
2) We'll enable your account for the smoothing credit at go-live and share a one-page reconciliation example to include with your internal forecast.
